$comment: The Astra plugin trust roots — public keys only, and there are none yet. `roots` is EMPTY because the ceremony in tools/keygen-root.sh has not been run: it is run once, by hand, on an offline machine, and its output is copied here afterwards. An empty root set is the correct state for a chain whose anchor does not exist, and astra-daemon behaves accordingly — it compiles in an empty PRODUCTION_ROOT_KEYS, so no trust.json verifies and no catalogue signature is believed. That is fail-closed, not a gap to be filled with a test key. See SECURITY.md.

notes.what_a_root_signs: trust.json, and nothing else. trust.json names the index signing keys and their validity windows, so an index key rotates without shipping a new Astra. A root signature never appears on index.json, on revocations.json, or on a plugin bundle.
notes.how_many: Two, generated in the same ceremony: one active, one reserve that is never used until it has to be. Both public halves ship in every Astra binary from day one, so replacing a root is a signature, not a flag day.
notes.the_anchor_is_the_key: Astra trusts this catalogue because a root key signed the trust.json that vouches for its signing key — never because of the hostname it was fetched from. `plugins.registry_url` is ordinary configuration and this catalogue may move hosts without changing a single trust decision. The daemon's verification path contains no hostname check and must not grow one.
notes.signature_construction: sig = Ed25519(root_private, SHA-256("astra.registry.trust/1" ‖ 0x00 ‖ JCS(signed))), where JCS is RFC 8785 over the document's `signed` member. The verifier supplies the domain string from its own compiled-in constant, never from the `schema` field of the file it is reading.
notes.test_keys: tools/testkeys/ holds two clearly-labelled TEST roots whose private halves are committed on purpose. They are not listed here and they are not production roots. astra-daemon can only compile them in behind `--features insecure-test-trust-roots` in a debug profile; asking for that feature in a release profile is a compile error.
notes.verifying_this_file: When it is provisioned, the fingerprints below are SHA-256 over the raw 32-byte Ed25519 public key — the same value tools/keygen-root.sh prints and the same value astra-daemon logs when a root signature verifies. This file is not itself signed; a self-signed root document proves nothing that the key compiled into the binary does not already prove. It exists so the two copies can be compared.
